tests.name: adapter install is consented, idempotent, merge-only and fully reversible; foreign hooks and backups are preserved
adapter refuses unparseable host settings, creates and removes its own file, and reports honest coverage for Codex
recorded Claude Code payloads flow hook -> spool -> drain -> Markdown evidence, idempotently, with a closed session and a queued retrospective
secrets are redacted before anything is queued or stored; hidden reasoning is never persisted; excluded content is never recorded
forged or unauthorized events are rejected and persist nothing: wrong principal, workspace, collection, registration, type, timestamp, ACL
overflow policy: a full queue evicts or drops low-value events first, counts what it dropped, and never blocks
fail-open: a missing, read-only, locked or corrupt vault never makes the hook fail or print; recording resumes when the vault is healthy
capture, drain and recall make no model call and need no provider
abandoned sessions are closed as INCOMPLETE with a clearly labeled partial retrospective; active ones are left alone
a later session of another authorized principal retrieves the record on demand; unauthorized principals get nothing
shutdown coordination: a detached drain started by session.end is observable, and a vault is only removed after it finishes
concurrent drains never fail on the lock, and the lock is always released with nothing left behind
a drain also picks up events that were enqueued while it was working (their own drain found the lock held)
real Claude Code: hooks installed by the adapter capture a real task; another principal recalls it; the host works with MDB broken or absent
real Codex CLI: trusted hooks pass actual lifecycle payloads, capture without memory-write instructions, and fail open
recent: newest first by event time with id tie-break, exact cursor paging, scope isolation and an upper time bound
time_range and timeline: timezone semantics, ascending order, evidence references preserved
progressive disclosure: index -> snippet -> timeline -> full fetch keep one identity, and token budgets are enforced with continuation
modes: grep, regex, keyword, links and auto work without a model; semantic and hybrid are explicitly unavailable; identity cannot be asserted
authorization: readers see only granted scopes, grants and revocations apply immediately, MCP rejects asserted identities
SQLite and filesystem recall agree, new commits are visible before any reindex, and a damaged index only degrades
CLI: mdb memory recent/search/timeline/get and capabilities work end to end as JSON
real Claude Code and Codex remote capture recover after HTTP outage and server restart

gaps.item: Independent authenticated agents cross-deliver passively across machines, including disconnect, retry, restart recovery and end-of-session retrospective/handoff
gaps.reason: Cross-machine transport: NOT_RUN.  Recent opt-in live run: PASS_WITH_LIMITATION, 1 passed/0 failed in 372963 ms. It used two actual CLIs and credentials through a stopped/restarted HTTP MCP server, including buffered replay, idempotency, SessionEnd and model handoff; limitation: clients/server were on one physical machine, so cross-machine transport remains NOT_RUN. Run MDB_REAL_REMOTE_HOST_TEST=1 with clients on separate machines for that evidence.

The live Codex 0.161.0 non-interactive `codex exec` dispatched SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse and SessionEnd, but did not dispatch Stop; assistant-message payload capture is therefore not evidenced for this invocation.
No adapter. MCP, CLI and SDK remain available.
No embedding provider or vector index; modes return CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE.
recent/timeline are manifest scans (O(authorized entries) in memory, no document reads); measured with the general benchmark in M5, not here.

gaps.item: Hook latency under a loaded host
gaps.reason: Fail-open and non-blocking behavior is tested (held writer lock, destroyed vault); per-hook wall time is dominated by Node start-up and was not benchmarked.

limitations: Events can be lost if the spool overflows, the host is killed before a hook runs, or SessionEnd is not delivered; each case is counted or swept, never blocking the host.
Assistant replies and read-only tool output are not captured by default.
Secret redaction is pattern based; unknown secret formats need an --exclude pattern.
